messages:
maria: FYI customers started seeing 502/504s against hosted inference at ~09:12 UTC, multiple tenant reports. Trace example: trace=3a7f9d. Seems correlated with billing token rotation window. Anyone else?

jon: I see a sharp spike in 504s from the edge (ingress nginx) starting 09:11:30 -> 09:18. Logs show upstream read timeouts and occasional upstream prematurely closed connection.

ash: can you paste a log snippet / request id?

maria: sure, one sample from nginx:```[09/Mar/2026:09:12:02 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2.0" 504 0 "-" "Go-http-client/2" "x-request-id: trace=3a7f9d; parent=abc" upstream: "http://10.2.8.12:8080/" while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.9.1.4, server: hosted-api``` Also saw 502s with `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream`.

devin: quick hypothesis: auth service was rotating tokens and auth-cache lookups spiked latency -> ingress pools drained/h2 keepalive exhaustion -> long-lived streams timed out. Could be auth latency + large auth header after rotation causing read stalls.

jon: metrics: auth-cache p95 jumped from 20ms -> 1.2s, h2 connection pool active streams hit configured max, connection window drift observed. Correlation with billing-bot rotation events: `billing-bot rotated key at 09:10:45`.

maria: customer repro steps they shared: 1) send streaming request to /v1/generate with large prompt (~60k tokens) 2) include Authorization header from SDK (post-rotation token) 3) request stalls then 504. They provided curl:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-4x","input":"...large..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0312-143 (severity: high). Notifying oncall.

ash: quick mitigation ideas: - increase upstream read timeout on ingress temporarily - add short-lived routing rule to route streaming calls to dedicated pool (if tenant has reserved capacity) - reduce default keepalive timeout to force connection churn less harmful

jon: applied temporary increase of `proxy_read_timeout` from 60s -> 120s for /v1/generate, and scaled auth-cache to +2 replicas. Watching.

devin: another data point: envoy upstream logs show RST_STREAM with error code 1 from model backend around same time. Might be model runtime hitting memory pressure on large prompts and killing streams, not just auth.

maria: customer updated: after our temp timeout increase they saw successful requests, but higher latencies and a couple of degraded responses. They want a postmortem and a way to avoid recurrence.

jon: next steps: 1) correlate model backend OOMs at 09:10-09:20 (eng-runtime) 2) add guardrails in hosted API for max prompt size per plan to prevent huge streaming payloads from exhausting model workers 3) look into auth-cache token rotation sequencing to avoid simultaneous cache misses (sticky old token accept for N seconds)

devin: repro checklist I ran locally: - replayed customer's large streaming payload to staging model pool -> reproduced tail 502s when worker restarted mid-stream - envoy logs show `upstream connection reset by peer` + model process restart. Command used: ```python tools/stress_stream.py --host staging-api --model rwd-4x --size 60000 --concurrency 3```

ash: I submitted a quick patch to the auth rotation logic (allow 30s dual-accept window) to reduce cache miss storm. Will open PR and run canary.

maria: billing-bot: can you confirm rotation timeline and whether the new header format added extra metadata?

billing-bot: rotation completed at 09:10:45 UTC. New token metadata adds `x-billing-tenant` header when present (optional). No forced header size change for all tenants.

jon: summary for postmortem: combined factors: large streaming requests -> model worker restarts/ooms -> upstream resets; coincident billing token rotation caused auth-cache miss storm worsening connection pressure at ingress -> 504s/502s.

maria: customer-facing remediation: - offered to route affected tenants to Dedicated for stable throughput for now - added temporary prompt size warning in SDK docs and increased server timeout - whiteboarding postmortem with eng-runtime and auth teams.

devin: tagging runtime and auth owners, opening followups: RUNTIME-254 (worker memory hardening + graceful drain), AUTH-789 (rotation dual-accept + cache warming).

jon: monitoring: I added alert for auth-cache p95 > 500ms and model worker restarts > 5/min.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll send update to customers in 30m and close escalation when all followups created. :thumbsup:
